_comment: REAL CAPTURED DATA, not an invented shape. This is the REG_TZI_FORMAT blob
Windows itself stores for 'Israel Standard Time', read out of the ADK
10.1.26100.2454 WinPE image's own registry - proof that WinPE CARRIES the
daylight rule it was never told to use.
Captured with (no mount; 7-Zip reads the WIM read-only):
7z x winpe.wim Windows/System32/config/SOFTWARE
reg load HKLM\HDTPESOFT <SOFTWARE>
(Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\HDTPESOFT\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Time Zones\Israel Standard Time').TZI
141 zones are present in that hive, so the database is complete in WinPE.
REG_TZI_FORMAT is 44 bytes: LONG Bias, LONG StandardBias, LONG DaylightBias,
SYSTEMTIME StandardDate (offset 12), SYSTEMTIME DaylightDate (offset 28).
SYSTEMTIME is eight UInt16: wYear, wMonth, wDayOfWeek, wDay, wHour, wMinute,
wSecond, wMilliseconds.
wYear IS ZERO IN BOTH, and that is the whole reason this defect can be fixed
at build time without baking a moment: a zero year means the RECURRING rule
'the wDay-th wDayOfWeek of wMonth', which the kernel evaluates against
whatever date the machine boots on - not a date somebody built an image on.
standardDate = October, week 5 (last), Sunday, 02:00
daylightDate = March, week 5 (last), Friday, 02:00
The ADK's WinPE database and a patched full-Windows host can disagree on the
week number - this host reads week 4 for March - because Israel's rule has
been revised. That is a difference between two Windows installations, not an
error in either, and it is why the rule is read rather than hard-coded.
